newsitem.title: India: Indian Oil Corp, Petronas in refinery talks.
newsitem.headline: Indian Oil Corp, Petronas in refinery talks.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) is discussing plans to build an export refinery with Malaysia's Petroliam Nasional (Petronas) on India's east coast, A.K. Arora, IOC's director of refineries and pipelines, said on Thursday.
In an interview with Reuters, Arora said the two national oil companies "have conceptualized the project as an export unit."
He said the production capacity and configuration of the refinery have not been finalised but he expected the output to be at least 120,000 barrels per day (bpd).
He said the plant could be operational early in the next decade.
Arora was speaking in Goa as oil producing and consuming nations gathered for a three-day international conference which opens on Friday.
In October, IOC said its investment in current energy projects was 100 billion rupees but that it planned to spend another 200 billion rupees on fresh projects.
At the same time, IOC said it had signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Petronas for a project, but released no further details.
Arora said the new IOC/Petronas refinery would probably be situated at Nagapattinam, on India's east coast, and would look to service markets such as Bangladesh, Burma, Thailand and Sri Lanka.
Around 75 percent of the output of the refinery would be geared to exports and the remainder for the domestic market.
The director said he expected IOC and Petronas would each take a 26 percent equity stake in the project, with the remaining portion to be sold to the Indian public.
The tie up is another step by Petronas to expand both its upstream and downstream operations abroad.
In September the company reported a rise in net profit of 48 percent to 6.76 billion ringgit for the year to the end of March.

Its most controversial investment has been a 30 percent stake in the Iranian Sirri oil field in the face of a U.S. boycott against Iran. The United States has not taken any action against Petronas, a U.S. ambassy official said in Malaysia in November.
In June, Petronas acquired a 30 percent stake in South Africa's Engen Ltd, which operates a 105,000 bpd refinery.
Elsewhere in the past year, Petronas has made a number of refining and marketing tie ups in countries such as Vietnam, the Philippines, China and Cambodia.
